captions: I am Orro. We call this roadside light a shrine, but it is also a relay: it passes the grid’s current from one stretch of road to the next. You can see its light, and I can measure its pulse. My grandmother taught me to listen before I touched it.

Some say the pause between pulses is the shrine taking a breath. I cannot measure a breath in copper; I can measure whether the pause repeats. The old name reminds me to pay attention, even when my instrument has no name for what I hear.
Touch the shrine once, then tell Marn in Wammigmig whether the road light answers. He is keeping a record of who depends on it.

hint:mission:orro:relay.text: Check the small relay beside Orro, then tell him whether its pulse holds. Inspect the relay beside Orro.
